# Keys AppKit keeps from the pane unless the pane claims them reach the
# program. AppKit offers a ⌃ or ⌘ key as a key equivalent first (the
# window's views, then the menus); one nobody takes there macOS may claim:
# ⌃Return opens the contextual menu (it's Claude Code's "send now"), ⌃/
# (⌃_, Emacs's and readline's undo) beeps and goes to another view, and a
# ⌘ key no menu has may become a command (⌘. is Cancel) that never reaches
# the pane as a key. keys-read.py prints what it read, in hex; with 1 the
# kitty keyboard protocol is on (as Claude Code turns it on).
type:python3 -I @ROOT@/tests/fixtures/keys-read.py 1
key:enter
wait:1.0
key-equivalent:ctrl+enter
wait:0.3
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect:GOT 1b 5b 31 33 3b 35 75 0d
type:python3 -I @ROOT@/tests/fixtures/keys-read.py
key:enter
wait:1.0
key-equivalent:ctrl+/
wait:0.3
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect:GOT 1f 0d
type:python3 -I @ROOT@/tests/fixtures/keys-read.py 1
key:enter
wait:1.0
key-command:cmd+.
wait:0.3
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect:GOT 1b 5b 34 36 3b 39 75 0d
